original.reason: The factor swap in step 3(a) is invalid: x^{-bn} and y^{-bn} are not adjacent, and moving x^{-bn} past y^{-bn} also crosses x^{-am}, for which no commutation is established. Consequently the later cancellation/reassociation is unsupported. Also, pairwise commutation of the displayed generators would suffice only after it has actually been validly proved.

judgment.reason: Its decisive “standard power-subgroup lemma” is exactly the substantive content needed, and the claimed derivation of the two commutator-power identities is merely asserted, not proved.

The coprime-power commutator lemma and its key identities are asserted through vague collection language. The hypotheses only give commutation within the respective power subgroups, so the omitted cross-term collection is a material issue.
The stated lemma is essentially the desired assertion after factoring out d. Its proof does not carry out the commutator expansions or justify the claimed conclusions c^r=c^s=1.
The elementary lemma contains the entire difficult step, while the asserted commutator calculation is not supplied. Thus it is not a complete rigorous proof.
